Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What was the most disgusting thing you have seen at an auto mechanic shop?
Answer: This may be cheating a bit but it actually occurred at an auto-electrician's garage. The guys who ran this garage were really nice. And I'm not just saying that as a form of courtesy. They were eerily pleasant to the point that I wondered if they were on some sort of drug or followers of some type of underground Eastern philiosphy/religion. They would never get impatient or irritated with you. There was a calming resonance in their voice that made you feel everything was going to be OK and they would listen to you with the utmost sympathy and understanding. Sometimes I would find myself wanting to visit them even though I had no electrical issues with my vehicle, just to bask in their warmth and friendliness. They were experts at their job too. As one would expect they were quite popular in the area. You would line up for hours to get a spot inside but it was worth it. Absolutely no one who was familiar with them would haggle, speak condescendingly towards or show any form of bad face towards them. That would be like sacrilege. However one guy had to be the one to disrupt the positive energy coming from our beloved hippie electrical-garage commune. In Trinidad we have this phenomenon called ‘wetman.’ A wetman is usually a vain but ignorant young man who thrives on attention. His life revolves around impressing easy women with a show of careless spending, flashy clothes and the official wetman badge of honour, his Nissan Tiida vehicle. For some inexplicable reason this vehicle is coveted by wetmen throughout the country, most likely due to the fact that it is one of the cheapest (foreign used) sedans available. Wetmen are also known to be notoriously cheap, uncouth and many of them live such a flagrantly hedonistic lifestyle, they are forced to secretly live in their Nissan Tiidas. In other words, a wetman is a scoundrel. One faithful day, a wetman joined the queue that we would form by parking outside the garage on a little road alongside the garage. In typical wetman fashion he had his gangsta music blasting at full volume the entire time he was parked. One of the apprentices would habitually pass to check on each person lined up outside to ask what was their problem. Doing this, they would find out who had simple problems that could be fixed at an instant, so he/she could be dealt with immediately and speeden the process. The apprentice went to the wetman who was blasting his music. The wetman only slightly lowered the volume to communicate with the apprentice. The apprentice had to tell the wetman to lower the music some more so he could hear him, which irritated the wetman. ‘My car giving trouble,’ Wetman said, ‘Everytime I switch off I have to ask someone for a jump start to start it back.’ The apprentice pulled out his multimeter and said, ‘Switch off the vehicle and lift the bonnet.’ The wetman scowled and in a venemous tone replied, ‘Brother. Like you not listening to what I saying? Switch off? You expect me to push this car all the way inside your garage?’ I was behind the wetman in the queue I was aghast at how stupid he was. Didn't he realize he was speaking to an actual electrician? Didn't he realize that the apprentice would find a way to get it started again? Wisely, the apprentice decided it was not worth it explaining all that to him and told him to wait until he gets a space inside the garage and the boss would personally deal with his vehicle. Wetman then resumed blasting his music much to the displeasure of myself and the apprentice who was now trying to ask me as to what was the issue I had. The apprentice had to go back over to the wetman and tell him again to lower the volume. ‘What da f**k boy,’ the wetman cried, ‘You all taking so damn long here and I can't listen to my tunes.’ He kept threatening to leave and I was hoping for him to make good on his threat but to my disappointment he remained. A half hour later we are both inside the garage. Realizing that the wetman was trouble, the apprentice wisely went to fetch the boss to deal with him. The boss arrived and Wetman stood outside his vehicle with arms folded. The engine was still running but the bonnet was lifted. Wetman squinted at the engine as though looking for some creature hiding somewhere that was causing his electrical problem. The boss approached and asked him what was the matter. Wetman scowled and replied, ‘I done tell yuh secretary what is the problem. Like you all dumb inside here?’ At that moment everyone's head turned towards Wetman's direction. Someone had blasphemed our precious garage! Everyone waited to see how the boss would handle it. No one ever witnessed any of the electricians lose their cool, especially the boss who was the kindest and most calm of them all. ‘Yes,’ the boss replied without any change of tone ‘Mike told me that you're getting ignition problems. I was just hoping to get some more information so I could know the best way to approach the problem.’ ‘The car not starting,’ Wetman uttered irritatedly, ‘What else you need to know? You is the electrician, not me. A whole hour I waiting outside, I going to lose out on a job I was getting.’ He then did what we Trinis call ‘steups’ which is the noise poorly raised people make to show disgust by sucking spit through your teeth. ‘Switch off the ignition let me run the tester through.’ Again Wetman's face scowled and he got defensive, ‘Brother,’ he growled, ‘I not switching off my engine. Last man I went by make me switch off the engine. He couldn’t fix my problem and I had to push my car out the road and ask someone for a jumpstart. That is failure. You have to fix my problem with the engine running!’ The boss stared at the apprentice and then glanced at the Wetman, who was clearly of a legendary level of stupidity as he stood there defiant and folding his arms. How is the boss going to deal with this one? Everyone was probably thinking the latter question. ‘I understand,’ said the boss calmly, ‘However if we operate on your vehicle while it's running we could destroy your circuits. The danger…’ The boss then paused for second and said, ‘Next Monday is the best day for you to come. We're getting a device that can work on vehicles while the engine is running without damaging anything. It's being shipped from China so give me a call Sunday evening to confirm when you're coming.’ Like magic, the little white lie worked and wetman accepted and left in a hurry to see about his hired job. Everyone breathed a sigh of relief when the ignoramus left. The next time I came, I enquired about the I individual and they happily informed me that someone must've solved Wetman's problem because he never did call or show up again. Or maybe he was offered a starring role in the movie below.

Question: Who was the rudest person you’ve ever encountered? And what was your response?
Answer: Some years ago I was working the late shift at my part time job doing pizza delivery. I was taking phone calls when a smug, off-putting voice was suddenly heard on the other end of the line. 'Are you hearing me? This is Michael Griffith. G-r-i-f-f-i-t-h.’ There was a second of silence as I registered that that the person didn't even bother to say 'Good Evening.’ I acknowledged that I could hear him and subtly mentioned that I could spell. I then proceeded to ask him for more information. 'I have been a regular customer to this restaurant for over 15 years. I like my pizzas done a special way. Are you listening……what is your name?’ 'Elijah sir.’ 'I want a veggie pizza. Listen to how I want it……Are you hearing me?……..I want the dough baked with the pizza sauce and cheese, nothing else added………are you writing this down?…….Then I want the raw veggies added after the pizza has been cooked. DO NOT COOK MY VEGGIES. I REPEAT. DO NOT COOK THE VEGGIES ON MY PIZZA.’ I tried my best to separate this man's condescending tone and my feelings towards him and mentally process exactly what it was he requested. We always got customers who felt entitled to have their pizza done in some special way. Either they wanted their pizza baked separate from all other pizzas or their dough must be of a certain grade or the pineapples must be cut from fresh fruit and not from our canned stock. Most of the time we ignored them and just gave them what they (and everyone else) were paying for. Most of the time they just wanted to feel bourgeois. This guy however was adamant that I make his pizza with raw veggies. What this guy didn't seem to realize was that these veggies were never freshly cut veggies. These were precut veggies sitting overnight in a plastic tub in a chiller, probably swarming with bacterial matter. Cooking these veggies in the oven was his only defense against E-coli. If he were to get sick from eating his beloved raw veggie pizza, he could hold us accountable and sue and I would be the one to get the blame. I diplomatically expressed to him that we couldn't make his pizza in such a manner, that it was a risk to his health and against the company's policy. In anger he asked for my name a second time. 'Listen to me young man. I am arriving in 15 minutes and if I do not see my veggie pizza prepared the way I want it, I am going to deal with you.’ He then hung up the phone. I explained what just happened to the cashier and she agreed with me that the guy was an idiot and that we couldn't give him a raw veggie pizza. I processed the pizza order as a regular veggie pizza and continued taking calls. Fifteen minutes later I'm in the back, about to head out on a delivery when I heard a smug but familiar voice bellowing out at front counter, 'WHERE'S THAT STUPID BOY NIGEL?’ I looked in front to see Mr. E-coli in the flesh. He looked exactly like how I imagined he would look; large, big-bellied and bespectacled. He was middle aged and greying, with a thick bottom lip that projected outwards in perpetual disgust at the world in front of him. I kid you not he looked like the human version of the obnoxious character Bubble Bass from SpongeBob. Immediately my entire physique and mental structure took to the offense. I literally wanted to clobber this idiot. However, I marched to the front counter to confront him and use all my powers of vocabulary to diplomatically explain to him that he was an idiot and that he was not getting a raw veggie pizza from this branch. As if to make himself as repulsive as ever, with him was a preteen girl (either his niece or daughter) with whom he tried to exaggerate how tough he was, by yelling and berating, mostly female minimum wage paid fast food workers. 'Listen to me,' he shouted at the cashier, 'Remove this pizza and get me what I ordered. I want to see that boy who took my order.’ He then spread a creepy smile over his face, turned to the little girl and cooed, 'You’re gonna taste the real way to eat pizza.’ The poor little girl looked like she wished she could disappear at the moment. Everything about the guy was just so off-putting in an incongruent sense. He was like a living, breathing 'Can you find all the things wrong in this picture’ cartoon brought to life. 'I'm the one who took your order sir,’ I said with seething rage as he glanced me, ‘And you can't get a raw veggie pizza.’ I saw him turn red. This was no longer about the pizza. This was about him proving himself to that little girl. 'You telling me what I can or can't get?’ he bellowed, 'You want me to knock you out?’ I stood there waiting for the tub of lard to attack when the manager flew out her office and came between us. In her best prepared monologue she explained she was sorry for his inconvenience. The manager told me to go to the back. In anger I listened as she explained the danger of consuming such a pizza but acquiesced to his demand. After I cooled down some minutes later I grabbed a delivery and en route to my motorcycle out front I spotted him shovelling away his bacteria ridden pizza in his mouth and commanding the little girl to do the same. He gave me a nervous sideglance as I passed, then continued goading her to finish her slice. I asked God to protect that little girl from getting sick and pleaded that He not allow more idiots like that man to multiply on this Earth.

Question: Have you ever come back to your vehicle only to find something quite unexpected?
Answer: I worked pizza delivery some years ago at a branch that was located in a rather iffy town. I used to park my vehicle at the tiny parking lot in the back. There was a dumpster that was located in the parking lot that attracted a lot of drug addicted homeless men who would scour the garbage for some odds and ends of food. One night we worked late and I stayed back after the store closed to give a ride to three ladies who would've been stranded waiting for taxis that late hour. I waited as they swept, mopped and balanced the cash register. An hour later they are finally done and we head to the back to the parking lot. Something looked odd about my pickup and upon closer inspection I saw that one of the glass windows at the door had been smashed with several tiny fragments of glass scattered in the back seat and floor. There was a gaping hole near the dashboard where my deck had once been located. The culprit had smashed a $600 glass window to get in and steal a beaten up, old car deck that probably had a $100 value at best. Having your car deck stolen is pretty commonplace around the world. However what was really unexpected was the reaction of the ladies with me. One of them chastised me for being such a fool for not parking my vehicle to the front of the store. The other found the ordeal somewhat amusing and told me that I should be happy that they didn't hotwire and steal the pickup. The third simply walked off and took a taxi without any comment. These were older women whom I had consistently remained after work to offer a ride being concerned for their safety. None of them even pretended to show any sympathy for what had happened to me. While I swept out the broken glass off the seats and floor, the remaining two stood there trading insider work-gossip and never made an attempt to assist me. I wanted nothing more than get in my vehicle and leave them there but I told myself that I would be the bigger person and go through with what I promised. I drove them homewards in silence. After that experience I stopped offering rides to stranded co-workers unless they were good friends. I used to feel so sorry for many of these ladies working fast food but I later realized that many of them are there not because of circumstances but because of their own ignorance and selfish attitudes. It took me a broken window and stolen deck to learn that lesson.

Question: Which boxer’s style do you find the most aesthetically pleasing?
Answer: Definitely The Lion Lennox Lewis. ‘The Lion’ is such an apt name because he does have a fighting style similar to a large cat. Lennox is a great tactician who uses his left jab to feint, taunt, displace and sometimes to smother and confuse. His left jab is like a diagnostic tool where he feels for the condition of the opponent and when the timing is right he unleashes powerful combinations. When facing shorter opponents he squats in a crab like posture and and uses his long arms and height advantage to monitor his opponents’ status, peering at them like a feline playing with its meal. If his opponent has some fight left in him and attacks, Lewis retreats in his crab like manner, smothering their offense with his own punches or jabbing them into a clinch. However he does not stick to this style. This style works for his shorter, less rangy opponents. When faced with opponents his own size and strength he's can successfully change styles from outboxer/boxer -puncher to brawler/pressure fighter. This is most evident in his fight with Vitali Klitschko where the bigger brawler’s (Klitschko) style was all wrong for Lewis’ clinical style. What I personally find pleasing about Lewis’ style is that you see the punches when they land, you see the frustration in his opponents face and the calmness in his. What I like about Lewis himself is that his boxing comes from a place of emotional maturity and self control. You see his method and you eventually see the results. His style is effective and shows a peek of the sportsmanship that lies in a sport that has its foundation in crude barbarity. Edit: If I could add the fact that Lewis is a seasoned chess player. I don't want to assume that this is a factor contributing to his typically calm and stoic demeanor, his emotional and ring intelligence. If I could dab in his personal life a bit, the fact that he is one of the few boxers to have relative success in his personal/family life, his ability to hang up his gloves and avoid any possible brain damage (as per his wife's plea) the avoidance of drug abuse, party lifestyle, scandal and controversy makes him (to me) an underrated role model in the world of sports on par with the likes of George Foreman. Just my 2¢.

Question: Have you ever walked out of an interview?
Answer: I didn’t walk out but I sure pissed the hell out of them and made it as awkward as possible. A cable company was looking for part time sales reps for their dishes. I already had a full time job but was looking for a sideline. They arranged for the interview to be at 9am. I came an hour early to their main office. The security had a sour look in his face and asked me what it is I wanted. I told him my name and that I had an interview for 9am. He looked at me as though I was talking jibberish and simply muttered that he didn’t know anything about that and directed me to the payments/customer service area to ask one of the people there where to go. I ignored the queue and walked directly towards the agents and the guard comes frantically running to me like a mama bird protecting its nest. ‘Follow instructions,’ he grunted loudly, ‘I told you to join the line.’ I wanted to bark at him that he never told me that and that he had to be the worse security guard I’ve ever encountered in my life, but of course that wouldn’t bear well for my interview. Suddenly a short pretty young lady passing by looked at me and said, ‘You’re Mr. Williamson?’ I said yes and she told me to follow her to the waiting area. She was professional but I found her a tad too detached. She didn’t ask me about my trip here or apologize for the confusion or anything. She led me to a corridor and and told me to sit by a row of chairs and that the sales supervisor would see me in a moment. She went into a room and came out with a tall, attractive lady with curly hair who looked no older than 24. They passed me without a glance and I assumed that they were both sales people. While sitting there a bunch of people kept passing and no one seemed to recognize my existence. They were all salespeople and mostly men. They came in to use the company phones to try and close sales and make a bunch of noise laughing and hooting afterwards with one another. Something about the vibe of the place just didn’t sit well with me. Around 9:45am the two young ladies passed by me again and without a word went back into the room they had left prior. A few minutes later the shorter one came out and called me in. She said the supervisor was ready to see me. I came in and saw a simple table in front of me where the tall girl sat with her fingers clasped staring at me. The shorter one sat to the side of her and they beckoned me to sit. Just looking at them I could sense that they were ladies who treated themselves well. Their clothes looked expensive, hair, nails and skin well treated, designer handbags etc. They were both very attractive and they knew it. The taller one proceeded to talk about sales and asked what the word ‘sale’ means to me. I kept mentioning how I prefer customer satisfaction rather than soliciting a sale and each time I did that she paused and reverted back to talking about how this job is concerned with hard selling and customer satisfaction can’t come if you don’t have customers. ‘We focus on sales only’ the shorter one chimed in. In my mind I sarcastically said to myself, ‘That’s a shocker.’ They then started discussing targets. They showed me a list of all the packages they were selling. They wanted to get the most expensive packages sold because they believe that people weren’t aware of how much better these were. They wanted to know if I had a problem focusing on selling only the expensive packages this month. They wanted me to lie and say basic packages were unavailable at the moment and that the next month I can sell basic like normal. I was starting to find them and this whole place tiresome. They clearly had values different from mine and I could see myself having spats with them in no time. I decided that I wanted out. However I wasn’t one to walk out on interviews as word gets around in this tiny country. I started asking about pay. ‘Commissions’ the taller one said. ‘Aren’t there any paying jobs,’ I replied, ‘With like a salary.’ They both looked at each other and the taller one replied that there were but that was a different division. I started telling them how I bought a dish from this company some years ago and how I thought it was garbage. I then said that my skills were so good that I could sell thousands of those garbage dishes to people who didn’t even have televisions. They both remained silent. I then said that I only worked on weekends and I don’t answer calls between 8 - 4 pm. They both looked at each other. ‘So Mr. Williamson’ the taller one said with a smile, ‘That’s the end of our interview. Thank you for your time and we’ll be contacting you before the end of the week.’ Without bothering to shake hands I headed out of the room like a man with a bladder control problem. Regardless to say I got a formal email from them a week later civilly explaining that I was unsuccessful with the interview.

Question: What did someone do to their home that you just can't understand?
Answer: My stepfather's parents owned a home that was a source of pride for the family. It was a rather large and stately hillside home that possessed several apartments on the bottom floor. The top floor was designed with several balconies that it could be used to host parties and events. The parents themselves had a good reputation with the neighborhood and kept the house in fine shape. They had three sons (one of which was my stepfather of course) all of whom couldn't be any more different than their parents in terms of reputation. When the parents died, they didn't make a will but rather implied to their sons that the oldest would be in charge while the younger ones would have living rights. At the times of their deaths the oldest was homeless and mentally unstable in Brooklyn after a long stint as a crack addict. The middle son (my stepfather), then used this opportunity to take reign, much to the displeasure of the youngest. He commanded the massive top floor to himself and rented the bottom floor apartments. At this time the area had become infused with drugs and crime and the house was starting to show signs of age. Deciding not to renovate it, (even though he's a skilled builder by trade) my stepfather decided to rent it to any old riffraff that comes by. In less than a year the house is infested with drug pushers, addicts, thugs and various people of ill repute whilst my stepfather sat like a Shantytown King overlooking everything from his balcony. The house started to become plagued with issues. Several of the toilets stopped working, many tenants had electrical issues, the front entrance was unusable as a a tree fell onto the front gate and destroyed it but was never removed, the cesspit was in dire need of flushing out so the entire house stank of this deep ghastly scent. The tenants decided to stop paying their rent. My stepfather, always a provocative individual, continuously hurled curses and threats towards his tenants for his rent money until one of them got fed up and assaulted him, threatening to kill him. My stepfather fled the house, never to return. The youngest son took this opportunity to have his daughter, a police woman, gather up her police friends and get rid of all the tenants. He took ownership of the house but by this time the house was so run down that he had no inspiration to do anything but reside on the top floor. He fell victim to lethargy and stopped paying bills and pretty soon the electricity was cut. He abandoned the house and lives with his daughter. The oldest son, deported and homeless, finally took residence in the dilapidated house. To answer the question as to what someone can do to their house that I just can't understand: I can't understand why parents would ever leave behind their house to be shared amongst the children.

Question: What was the best era of your life?
Answer: I had a happy childhood. My best era had to be the mid 90s to early 00s. My brother and I were introduced to cable television which my mother wisely subscribed to to distract us from the negative influence of the local boys from the Government projects we grew up in. It’s a good thing she did because one of those boys got killed involved in gang related activities while the other two are in jail. Though my brother and I would stare at the tube sometimes sixteen hours a day (during holidays) we were still far more active than today’s generation as we would go bicycling, exploring, kite-flying, football and sometimes cricket. Chasing and catching butterflies was still fashionable. Also catching crickets, grasshoppers and if you were lucky you would catch a praying mantis and put it to fight someone’s champion mantis. The poor creature would be lucky to be alive when is was time for the fight. I mastered grabbing fat toads and launching them into the sky to the delight of the boys around me. I never understood why even the toughest of boys were afraid to do this and was proud of my skill, until I learned why: frog piss. Saturdays were magical because of the deluge of quality cartoons, especially if you had cable. Once a cartoon had karate, missiles, endless shooting, things that transformed, people that kept getting more and more powerful, magic, snot, naked butts, muscles, sexual innuendo, school-related humour or based on a video game you bet your bottom dollar my brother and I watched it. Some of the worst pseudo-macho, dumb-kid cartoons in history were made in the 90s: However there were still lulls of boredom every here and there. This changed with the introduction of the first Playstation. You had to make friends with kids in your school that you didn’t necessarily like so much once word got out he/she had a Playstation because now you could trade games with that person. As the 90s came to an end, puberty came galloping on a horse to demand that I turn off the TV and Playstation and start focusing on the fairer sex. Luckily my cousin David migrated from Scotland to Trinidad and with his cash and my brother’s street smarts, we undertook several missions to get laid through clubbing, playing pool in trendy bars, religiously attending house parties, providing/consuming liquor etc. All of these missions failed miserably but we had fun anyway. Thus our lives revolved around making plans to get laid, failing, dusting our shoulders and enjoying each other’s company watching TV, playing video games, fishing or just plain old hanging out. Then David got his first girlfriend, was stricken with the worst case of ‘whipped’ and that awful scourge of puberty turned us all into taller, deep-voiced, acne riddled young men of differing mindsets and we gradually began to drift away from each other with this awful phenomenon called ‘discovering our identity.’ Now we are three completely different human beings with vastly different goals and perspectives in life. We respect each other, love each other and most of the time enjoy each others’ company but far gone are the days where we were a unit. I do yearn for those days but c’est la vie.

Question: What does a $1,500,000 house look like where you live?
Answer: Like the house the average lower-middle class bloke lives in. In Trinidad house prices are notoriously inflated. Real estate agents will tell you it's all about supply and demand but in reality it is because there are no checks and balances to the real estate sector. The above image is of a house built and sold by a private developer. Nothing looks outstanding about it. Heck, the owner didn't even bother to take a good photo of the house when the grass develops nicely and in nice weather to show off its mustard paint job. This house looks like how most Government commissioned, detached, single family housing units look like. A 5000 sq ft, 2–3 bedroom cookie cutter nestled amongst a swarm of others like it as far as the eyes can see. It's not unlikely that the guys who built the privately sold house are the same ones awarded the contracts to build the Government properties. Conflict of interest? Maybe. Will the private developer extend a lot of effort to his private development which is monitored by public opinion, customer satisfaction and subject to legal recourse? Yes. Will the private developer extend the same effort to a big fat Government contract whereby he's unsupervised in the making of hundreds of matchbox style cookie cutters, can bribe public officials to cut corners and is shrouded from public opinion as all fault is levied towards 'the corrupt government?’ Not so much. In essence, $1.5 mil in TT dollars can get you a generic matchbox style house with a tiny piece of yard to plant some flowers/herbs. You can apply through the Government if you have chronic problems in regards to finances and all it takes is just bending over backwards to show political allegiance and screaming to the heavens how hard your life in a gross public display. You can do that or be put on a waiting list and expect to be responded to in at least 25–30 years. When you do get your $1.5 mil Government house don't be so quick to celebrate. Crime, shoddy infrastructure and utilities and poor environmental planning are rampant in Government housing projects. So maybe a privately developed $1.5 mil house is the better option? With the private housing developments, there has been a growth in unapproved or downright illegal developments by unscrupulous developers. The house in the very first photo could seem like a pretty decent option but bear in mind these three possibilities. So in conclusion, in Trinidad $1.5 million can allow you to pick your own poison when it comes to housing.

Question: Why do people think Midsommar is a good horror movie? When I'm watching the movie, I didn't think it's scared even a bit.
Answer: If you go to watch Midsommar simply to get 'scared’ then you are in for a disappointment. It may not scare you in the sense that a knife wielding, mask wearing stalker/killer may or an evil, spectral entity that comes after you through your television but it may build feelings ranging from discomfort to dread to shock. It does not rely on fantastic and nightmarish tropes: ghouls, monsters and masked murderers etc. It doesn't condescend to our primitive childhood fears of a single creature/person out to get us (typically in the darkness of night). Most generic horrors play to our primitive childish fears: unwholesome locations, darkness, ugliness, being alone, unexplainable phenomena, pain, danger, the unknown etc. Midsommar does the opposite we are treated to a sunny, picturesque location full of wide open fields, brightly painted buildings and smiling beautiful people. Midsommar is not traditionally ‘scary’ because none of the characters are villains/monsters. None of the acts commited are evil when viewed in a purely cultural context. The film allows you to ponder on the cruelty and barbarism of several centuries past and at the same time offers a critique as to whether the self-centred, indifference that is characteric of our modern times is any better. Midsommar is a slow burning, psychological horror. It is one of the most disturbing movies I've seen in a long time, let alone one of the best. Ari Aster's directing style had been compared to Stanley Kubrick and I can really see the influence from The Shining, another slow burn, psychological horror. The story involves a young woman who recently suffers from a personal tragedy going to rural Sweden with her boyfriend and his college friends and witness/partake in the pagan Midsommar festival held once every 90 years. Little to their knowledge the participants take the festival a little more seriously than to their liking. I consider Midsommar more resonating and effective than 99% of the horror movies out there. If it doesn't scare you then too bad. There's a whole bunch ghouls and psycho killer movies out there for your liking.

Question: Can you give an example of a TV program you watched as a kid and thought it was cool or sophisticated, but seeing it as an adult you think it is dumb or appalling?
Answer: Tales From the Darkside. Dum dum da da………..Dum dum da da My brother and I would stay up late at nights watching Sci-Fi (now SyFy) just to hear that chilling intro. It was absolutely terrifying to hear those eerily innocent yet menacing keyboard notes accompanied with this ominous voiceover and the placid shot of trees, rivers and rural farmhouses suddenly melt into a distorted final image and caption. (Nothing beats the horror aesthetic of late 80s/early 90s television and film.) We would play a game to see who could sit and watch the intro in its entirety without running into the bedroom or hiding behind the couch. Neither of us succeeded. But it was thrilling nonetheless. I wish the show itself was thrilling though. The ‘tales,’ quality-wise, ranged from uninteresting to appallingly corny. Take a look at some screenshots and be the judge.

Question: As a man, what things do women do that creep you out?
Answer: My biggest creeping peeve about women (well some women) is their obsession with their image, especially in regards to marriage. Imagine a guy in a bar lamenting, to anyone willing to listen, about his failing marriage. Imagine confronting Jimmy about seeing him walking hand in hand with another woman. Jim comes clean and explains that he's seeing someone else because he's unhappy with his spouse. Now imagine these two characters in reverse as females rather than males. I'm sure now the scenarios are a lot harder to imagine. It always astonishes me how some women could go to such extremes to keep up the image that they are in a satisfactory marriage and life is so great for them. Among his fellow men, at the slightest nudge, a man would confess about his marital troubles and broken home. Among her fellow women, some women can be tied to the stake with the threat of being burnt alive, but would never confess that her marriage is in shambles. I once got involved with a co-worker who was in the process of separation and divorce from her husband. The relationship had to be kept secret because she didn't want her female peers to learn of her divorce and ugly child support battles. Frankly I don't think those female coworkers could've given a fart about her image but she fought tooth and nail to protect it, creating high fantasy scenarios of what the family did over the weekend that would give Tolkien a run for his money. I worked with another women who bragged about how great her husband was and how he brought lunch for her every day. She is currently in jail for his murder. It's a trait that some women have that to this day I can't understand. They would gush about planning to go to the Bahamas in the summer with the kids and the 'huzzy’ when the fact is that 'huzzy’ is in the Bahamas with his mistress and she is dating the police officer who plans to trap him for unpaid child support when he returns. Would she admit any of this to her peers. Never. But in the end everyone usually finds out the truth about her marital situation and she looks like the world's most deluded fool. But still it's just a creepy fact that so many women are obsessed with their marital image to the point of fanatical delusion and even self destruction.

Question: Does your country have an icon whom you believe is grossly overrated? Is there someone who is underrated that should replace him/her?
Answer: Trinidad is not known for its success in the world of literature but whenever the topic comes up, this guy is always mentioned. V.S. Naipaul (1932 — 2018) If you go to Ireland to ask an average bloke who they think is the greatest modern Irish writer your mind might probably presume they will say it's this guy. James Joyce (1882 — 1941) But it's far more likely this guy would be the answer. Brendan Behan (1923 — 1964) But who's that guy? He looks like a fool. Isn't Ulysses by Joyce considered the greatest modern novel of all time? Ulysses by Joyce is always mentioned in every greatest English language novels list. Who are the critics who normally create these lists? Well duh. The English. Joyce wasn't particularly admired by his fellow men during his lifetime. Constantly imposing self exile to Switzerland and France, he wrote high-brow, experimental novels that condescended and stereotyped Irish nationalists and appealed to the literary elites in Paris, London and New York. His funeral in Zürich, Switzerland was ignored by the Irish diplomats residing there and was attended only by the British Consul. The Irish government refused to repatriate his body Behan was almost the opposite. He was a staunch Irish Republican, an IRA member, an unapologetic alcoholic, was fluent and sometimes wrote in Irish. He was working-class witty, impulsive and had a larger that life attitude that led to his untimely death at age 41. He was the hard-drinking, self-destructive patriot that Joyce would mockingly caricature. In other words he definitely wasn't someone the English hierarchy at the time would think too fondly of. His funeral was then considered one of the biggest Irish funerals since Michael Collins. What does all this have to do with V.S. Naipaul? It's almost the exact same scenario in Trinidad literature. Naipaul was a writer of some talent who basically turned his back on his country, played monkey for the British by writing in some imitation Dickensian style about how backwards his home country was and in return was given citizenship, a slew of affirmative action awards and false praise. Having over ten years experience working in public libraries, I can say with confidence that the one of the best lanes to reshelf is the Fiction NAI - Naipaul section. The books there are always untouched. Anytime someone actually borrows a Naipaul book it is either a tourist or some eccentric literature snob looking for something to brag about. Otherwise the dateslips in his books are spotless clean of due date stamps. His early works portray Trinidadians as either cartoonish simpletons living in dirt huts or petty street scamps and beggars in the city and his later work reeks of cynical, self praise. His prose in my opinion is dull and many times hard to comprehend with his constant attempt at stretching out a sentence or finding a big, archaic word to replace small one. Here is a sample from his book The Mimic Men (1967) "Coconut trees and beach and the white of breakers seemed to meet at a point in the distance. It was not possible to see where coconut turned to mangrove and swampland. Here and there, interrupting the straight line of the beach, were the trunks of trees washed up by the sea. I set myself to walk to one tree, then to the other.” I almost fell asleep just copying and pasting that. Why the second unnecessary 'and’ in the first line? Why not say ' foaming waves’ instead of 'white of breakers?’ Who on Earth says 'I set myself to walk…?’ It sounds like the voiceover for another pseudo artsy Chanel advertisement. These types of pompous passages could be find throughout his ouvre. Naipaul is to many Trinidadians the classic sell out. His personality was not known to be a pleasant one. He proudly exclaimed his distaste for his country calling being born in Trinidad a mistake. After winning the Nobel Prize in 2001 he failed to recognize Trinidad in his press release. For his return trip to Trinidad he was asked to visit several schools and advise young aspiring writers. He requested to be paid and was irritable and condescending, basically telling impressionable young men and women that his novels were above their intelligence. He was a bastard in his personal life. He used his first English wife as a stepping stone as she fervently sought to get his work published in England. When he got his big break he got on his high horse and chased after women around the world, coming home to verbally and mentally abuse her, calling her sexually unattractive. He did not mourn for her when she died in 1995 as much as he mourned the death of his cat. To me he was nothing but a pretentious, overrated curmudgeon and variations of this sentiment is shared throughout the island. So who is underrated and should take his place? This dapper young fellow here is called Samuel Selvon (1923 —1994) He is very much the Brendan Behan of Trinidad in my honest opinion. Selvon wrote as a form of expression, not to kiss ass and self praise. He was proud of his roots and gave a thrilling, funny heartfelt and completely unbiased account of Caribbean 'Windrush’ emigration to England in the 1950s, complete in local dialect in his masterpiece The Lonely Londoners. He did not try to sound like Dickens while bashing his homeland and praising how great England is like Naipaul but his book made a great impact and is considered a modern classic. He died of respiratory failure while in the Piarco airport returning to Trinidad in 1994. It's almost as though he held back death until the moment he touched home soil. Question: What's something on an employee's first day that sets off red flags?
Answer: In my second year at my current job, a lady was hired to replace my senior who had resigned. The job was in a public office and for the most part was quite easy going. Somebody off the streets could learn the essentials in just a few hours. The lady who came had seniority and several years more experience than me working at a different branch. I therefore expected her to have a wealth of knowledge and experience to share with me. 'How does this work again?’ 'Did I do this right?’ 'How about you be the one to do that? You're so good at it.’ 'Can you show me how to do (such-and-such) again?’ The lady transferred from a location that had the exact same type of system and technology as mine yet she had not a clue how to do anything! How was this woman in a senior position? She didn't know anything about the job. Was she dumb? A week of 'training’ had passed and she didn't really learn anything and had to be supervised at all times. Before I could find out how it was that she was so slow she suddenly vanished. She stopped turning up at work and calls to her phone went unanswered. I sent an email to HR explaining that she had gone AWOL. They gave some half-assed reply. A few months later, after she had long been forgotten, I get a frantic letter from HR saying that they have been paying her salary and they've just become aware that she has not been turning up to work. ‘No shit,' I say in my mind. HR investigates and finds out that she had accepted another job elsewhere the entire time and was gladly accepting two salaries. HR demanded that she return the unearned salary. She said she would but she was going through financial distress at the moment. She never returned a cent. HR washed their hands of the matter and kept it hush hush. Turns out she wasn't dumb at all. So my answer to the question 'what sets off red flags on an employee's first day?’ Playing dumb.

Question: What are the best and the worst movie posters ever?
Answer: The Best You know how as a child practically anything could impress you. You see Bio-Dome (1996) as a 10 year old and Pauly Shore is the greatest comedian to walk the face of the Earth. Or, nothing is as terrifying as this scene in Ernest Scared Stupid (1991) And of course, no science-fiction could match the imaginative, voyeuristic spectacle of Jane Fonda in Barbarella (1968). But then you grow older and revisit these movies to feel that same sense of awe as a child only to ask yourself 'Did I really like this s**t!?’ It happens to me all the time. One movie that didn't disappoint when returning to it was Terminator 2: Judgement Day (1991). I managed to get to see it in cinema as a 5 year old with my family and I can't forget the moment I glanced upon that iconic poster of Arnie clad in leather jeans and jacket, straddling a Harley Davidson while clutching a shotgun with one eye glowing red amidst a cold, steely blue background. Let's look at it again. It sent exciting shivers down my spine as a toddler and it still manages to have the same effect as a grown ass man. The Worst Funny enough, the worst movie poster was viewed at the same time I viewed the best. Don't Tell Mom The Babysitter's Dead (1991) was a double feature with Terminator 2. Thankfully it was shown after Terminator so we left within ten minutes of the movie. I remember staring at the poster wondering what the hell was happening here? I remember bursting into tears at the poster and telling my mother I didn't like this movie. She reassured me by telling me we wouldn't have to watch it if I don't like it and sure enough we left the cinema. I've never attempted to watch it since then and it probably maybe a damn good movie but that horrid poster still brings out the scared toddler in me.

Question: What was your cringiest moment with a boss?
Answer: Ms. B was a former supervisor of mine in a Government building I worked. She was a lady in her early 50’s. She was a nice person but was an eccentric and an introvert to the core. When things were slow she would stay isolated in her office, playing chess online or taking a nap. When she came out of her office her only conversation would usually be short, irritable grumbles about random stuff that annoyed her about the job and the typical ‘can’t wait for the weekend/payday’ talk. Then she would return to her idle privacy. Mary, a co-worker of mine, observing that our supervisor had so much free time on her hands, decided to enroll in an online course. Mary thought it fair she perform her duties during the morning and after lunch work on her online studies. Ms. B began observing this and one day, while stepping out to grab lunch, made a snide comment towards Mary’s direction: ‘Lunch break is just an hour. I don’t want to report people who like to come to work and do their own thing.’ Ms. B’s grumble was directed towards Mary but in a most blunt and condescending manner. Mary, being a woman of passion, could not take such a hypocritical statement without taking some kind of action. For days, she plotted on how she would give Ms. B a piece of her mind; how dare she? Ms. B who does practically nothing, making accusations of others doing as such. They say it’s only thieves who are always paranoid that everyone wants to steal from them. Such and such was the rantings of Mary for that evening. The day Mary decided she was going to confront Ms. B about the statement, something strange happened. Ms. B, in a seemingly good mood, had come out of her office and was helping visitors and getting involved in the day to day operations of junior staff like myself and Mary. Then Mary observed something that made a Cheshire grin spread across her face. ‘Elijah,’ she said, ‘Look at Ms. B’s pants.’ I looked. Ms. B was wearing a beige colored work-pants. Nothing seemed out of the ordinary until I observed that there was a wet, red spot observable from the back, around the crotch area. I stared aghast. Ms. B didn’t seem to notice her period came down on her and clearly had no protection against such an event. She must’ve assumed that her menopause came to an end and periods were now a thing of the past for her. Some of the people she was dealing with seemed to have observed her predicament also but looked as though they felt too awkward to say anything about it. I looked at Mary and said, ‘We should tell her about it.’ ‘No,’ Mary replied, ‘Not right now.’ Mary waited until the very last visitor left the building and the usual evening lull began. Ms. B went into her office and closed the door. I watched as Mary went up to the door, knocked and entered. ~~~~~~~~~~~ Ten minutes later Ms. B, with all her belongings on her, sped past me while uttering, ‘I have to deal with a matter.’ She hastily left the building. Mary told me that when she explained the situation to Ms. B, the look that came upon Ms. B’s face was nothing short of the deepest dread and horror. That for a second she wore the facial expression of a convict at the gallows. I could not help but empathize with the level of cringe Ms. B must've felt on her way back home. Mary got her poetic justice. If she were really mean she could’ve spread the word about the incident through the entire building but the slight torture was enough. Mary and Ms. B began to develop a meaningful relationship after the incident. In other words they started to scratch each other’s back. Maybe it was some sort of neurotic subconscious agreement they both made, as in reminding each other ‘You got me covered right?’ Maybe the situation gave Ms. B a slice of humble pie? I don’t know. What I do know is that to this day I don’t understand women.

Question: Is it morally wrong to want to read Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf?
Answer: I’ve no desire to read it but if someone suggested that by reading it, it would prove that I’m secretly a neo-Nazi then I would have a hearty laugh. I’ve read Venus is Furs. I’m not a masochist or into any form of BDSM. I’ve read The Doors of Perception. I haven’t ingested LSD nor have I been tempted. I’ve read Trainspotting. I’m not in the least bit curious to try heroin or any drug 1000 times more powerful than my greatest orgasm. Read The Stranger and Crime and Punishment. I was never tempted to kill someone for the heck of it. Read The Sun Also Rises and I still hate bullfighting to this day. Read all the Harry Potter novels and I'm still not inspired or influenced by witchcraft. I've read Lolita. I don't sympathise with pedophiles and hebephiles. I've read 1984. I think my Government is way too stupid to suppress my thoughts and actions. My point is I've read these books because I enjoy reading. If I don't enjoy the story, find it uninteresting or dislike the author's writing I simply put the book down. The only people who will get influenced by Mein Kampf or any of the books I've listed above are people who already believe the values and ideas they think the book suggests. The book is simply greater affirmation (or for some people, a good excuse) for enacting on these desires.

Question: What is the most offensive thing you've been told while out on a date?
Answer: A decade ago, I went on a date with someone I met on a dating website. I considered myself witty back then and a good few of my jokes had a sarcastic element to them. I met someone on the dating site who seemed to greatly appreciate deadpan quirkiness and sarcasm. She seemed to appreciate it a bit too much than is healthy for the average human. We arranged to meet at the mall. When we saw each other her eyes flitted away from mine and she stared at my shoes. 'That's the shoes you came to see me in?’ She then gave a soft yet caustic 'huh huh huh’ laugh to herself and began what would be a series of rolling eyes at everything that was said. I didn't understand what she meant. The shoes were almost new and were my best pair of sneakers. In fact, compared to her I was overdressed as she wore a rather unflattering suspender-skirt combo and an old pair of sandals. Minus the afro she looked a lot like the photo below but far more unkempt. I decided to ignore the comment. I asked her if she wanted to see a movie and she immediately made this whistling noise and started to go off about mindless dribble that Hollywood dishes out. I sort of agreed with her but at the same time her anti-Hollywood rant came across a bit on the pretentious side. We basically walked around the mall, her making random sarcastic comments about anything in her field of vision and me trying to agree with what she said and keep the conversation flowing. When we parted ways and I went homewards I did a quick mental audit of the date and my conclusion was that she definitely was not my cup of tea. However I told myself that maybe she probably suffers from some sort of anxiety and that's why she behaved so strangely. Maybe I ought to give her a chance. I called to tell her that I enjoyed our time and to find out if she was back home safe. 'Calling to see if I'm home safe?’ she replied, 'Bro. That's so corny. That's like men from the 50s.’ I could hear her faint 'huh huh huh’ laugh and could envision her rolling her eyes. I couldn't help but notice a strong pang of irritation develop within me. I put that aside and we spoke for a bit and ended up agreeing to meet her after she finished her classes the following day (she did a Degree in Computer Science). I told myself that with a little patience she would drop that caustic quirkiness of hers and start showing more warmth . I bought a rose for her and travelled to her school. I told myself what girl wouldn't love a man greeting her outside her class, well dressed and holding a rose for all her peers to see. Being that her class was due to over in a few minutes I basically ran up the street. When I arrived at the school, I called her phone to no avail. I told myself that her class was probably still in session. Then I saw a bunch of students filing out and I knew that she had to be among them. I saw her at the back, looking particular slovenly staring at me with her usual vacant stare. 'Oh my God.’ I saw her mouth the words as I moved towards her with the rose. However she mouthed it in distaste as though I were brandishing a slimy toad. As I reached within earshot she said the single most offensive thing I've ever heard someone mutter to me during a date. 'I was hoping you didn't come.’ This was followed by her 'huh huh huh’ laugh and rolling eyes. The irritation from the day before changed to anger. I tried to put aside the statement as another of her offbeat quirkiness and told her passionately about my hasty journey to get to her and how I ran up the street so as not to have her waiting. 'Dude,' she replied, 'That's psycho talk. Shut up.’ I paused and looked at her for a long while. Her supposed sense of humour was truly starting to rub me the wrong way. It sounded like a joke but came across like a vent fashioned into a rude and unfunny joke. She then talked about how she saw phone calls but intentionally disregarded them in the hopes that I would go away. She then mentioned that she saw me running up the street like a madman with a rose in my hand and felt so embarrassed. I remained silent. It was now a code red. Either I give her a piece of my mind or bow gracefully and leave. I opted for the latter and waited for a good civil moment to depart. 'You look like the type who doesn't go anywhere,' she continued, 'Seeing how you just ran through the streets just to see me from class you probably don't go out much. My ex boyfriend was a DJ. I used to get in to all the parties for free. He wasnt much to look at but a little sex now and again and I got into all the exclusive parties…..even aboard yachts. You know what a yacht is right?’ I remained silent. 'Dunno why I'm telling you all this………Look at you.You look like you want knock my head off don't you. Huh huh huh.’ It then dawned upon me that this girl was a twisted individual. This wasnt some quirky sense of humour. This was someone who got their kicks off of provoking others. Whatever hurt she experienced from those she loved in the past, she clearly wanted to exact that hurt on innocent people around her. When she arrived at her taxi stand I stood and waited in silence until she got into one. 'Well look at you,' she said in a last desperate attempt for a reaction from me, 'My knight in shining armour... You should maybe think about buying a car……it's kinda lame that…' The taxi driver sped off without waiting for her to finish what she was saying, probably cognizant that she was someone full of shit. I went home proud of myself that I didn't give her the reaction she desired. I deleted my account on the dating site. After that encounter I became far more conservative towards the use of sarcasm in humour and communication. I've been attracting much more likable and attractive females ever since that minor adjustment. So everything truly is a learning experience.

Question: Why is reading so important?
Answer: Imagine this. You are with some friends on a fishing excursion in the Mediterranean sea. Miles away from the nearest harbor your yacht begins to sink. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) Another scenario. You are in a cabin in the Swiss Alps. An avalanche occurs and buries your cabin under twenty feet of snow. Your phone has enough juice to make one call. Who do you call? A) B) Final scenario. You have been drugged unconscious and abducted by traffickers who want to harvest your organs. Your kidnappers are taking you to a foreign land in which you cannot decipher the language, pinpoint the culture or recognize the terrain. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) If you chose ‘B’ for all the scenarios, congratulations, you are alive. If you chose ‘A’ for any scenario, you are most likely dead. The characters pictured under 'A’ are men who are extremely well-read. Ken Jennings — Record holder for the longest winning streak on Jeopardy. Karl Marx — Founding father of Marxism, a proponent of communism. Bill Nye — A mechanical engineer and popular television presenter, comedian and educator. The characters pictured under ‘B’ are men who are extremely well-read but also have a lot of worldly experience. Joseph Conrad — Polish born English author, explorer and ship captain. Jack London — American author, sailor, journalist and former Klondike prospector. Richard Francis Burton — English explorer, translator, linguist, historian and writer. This is not slight against the achievements of the characters under 'A’ it's just that the fellows under 'B’ have allowed for the knowledge they've amassed through reading to inspire them towards physical action which in turn develops experience and skill. Ken Jennings and Bill Nye might be able to tell you what is the distance of each planet in the Solar system from the sun in less than a minute but that doesn't mean NASA would aggressively pursue them. Marx, if he were alive, could write a 1000 page book on why he thinks 20th century communism failed but do you think Maduro or Castro would’ve employed him as an advisor? Group A are individuals of impressive intelligence but any logical thinking individual would recognize that Group B is superior in regards to worldly applicability. So to answer the question, reading is important to gain knowledge. Reading is very important, but not as important as the ACTION that it stimulates.

Question: What are some of the most stunning yet most terrifying images?
Answer: When I was but a preteen, I came across a book of the supernatural and under 'The Flying Dutchman’ an image of this painting was included. Something about the image haunted me for years to come. Firstly was the strangely breathtaking yet ominous sunset that gave me a eerie 'deathbed’ feeling. This made the fact that the ocean was in the midst of a freak storm incongruous and unearthly. It's as if the appearance of the ghostly ship in the sky had some sort of cosmic power over the Earth. The men, clearly on the verge of being drowned, seem to be in a trance at the surreal beauty of this golden phantasm. I never discovered the name of the artist, in fact I never came across the image for the next 20 years. The image randomly passed through my mind recently and I decided it was time to end the mystery. With a simple Google search I found out that the artist was an eccentric 19th century American artist called Albert Pinkham Ryder (1847 — 1917). His oeuvre is quite fascinating as most of his paintings employ that haunted, moody atmospheric theme. I think his work is quite fascinating and worth checking out. I think he is grossly underrated so please allow me to share a few more images of his works. All photos courtesy Google.

Question: What's the most ruthless thing a new boss has done to show he/she is in charge?
Answer: My very first job was doing construction labor for my stepfather when I was 17. He was a foreman and a downright bastard of a foreman. The guys on the site would refer to him as Pharaoh. When I told him about that nickname he laughed heartily and seemed proud of himself. He worked everyone to the bone. He pretended he had the highest standards when he looked at the work his men did. He boasted that he helped construct mega projects in Brooklyn and Vermont and that the house that we were building must 'shine like his mansion' (even though in reality he lived in a wooden shack with no electricity as my mother had recently kicked him out. The men all respected him though. There wasn't a job that he cussed out a laborer or mason for that he couldn't do himself. For a thin, wiry 5′9 guy he was full of strength and energy. He loved to display this whenever he claimed we were taking too long and would grab someone's shovel and mix mortar or concrete effortlessly as though he was whipping up mashed potatoes. He once gave me the duty of tearing down a large 10ft mound of earth and then transporting the dirt to fill behind a retaining wall. All day I spent labouring and when the sun began to set, barely half of the mound was done. It was too solid for me to break. He dropped some F and C bombs at me, grabbed my pickaxe and with a few solid strikes the mound was no more. I was utterly stunned. However he was utterly provocative, insensitive and and sometimes seemed borderline insane. He would get into these mood swings and yell at us to get off our lazy c**ts and work even if a heavy shower of rain was falling. He wanted to pick a fight with a mason when none of the bricks were laid, not realising that the bricks weren't delivered to the site yet. He would stamp around ceaselessly yelling the F word whenever there was a setback, even if it was no fault of the workers. Sometimes we wondered if he was on drugs. He seemed to have an intense hatred of seeing his workers do nothing and in his tantrums he would flings brooms and buckets our way commanding us to ‘dont sit and gape, clean the f**king place or something.' But all of this were just gimmicks to stoke fear and intimidate everyone. He believed that in his field that was the only way to get the job done. However, the worst thing he ever did to instill fear and show power was when he forced the laborers (mostly young, naive men like myself) to climb planks of wood to get to the foundation floor. He thought it was better than spending money renting some scaffolding. One of the new laborers (a young man who seemed mentally slow) fell off the planks while carrying bricks and received an awful bleeding gash on his elbow, rendering him unable to work hard. Pharoah inspects the wound and gets angry. 'No, no no,' he said solemnly, “Just go. Get out of here.’ The young man pleaded that he could work but my stepfather fired him on the spot, without as much care as to offering a bandaid. Looking at the guy I could see that he came from poverty and probably had little to no education, let alone the fact that he was mentally slow. I thought the rest of the labourers would revolt against him for their friend but Pharoah knew how to please his peons. Beers. Every Friday he treated the boys to drinks on his bill after work at a bar in the closest town. The men would get stone drunk and cheer to their master. They never realised that some of the money he used to buy these drinks was the money he made off cutting costs and overworking them.

Question: What 1980s movies were huge at the time but are now almost forgotten?
Answer: The Abyss (1989) As a child of the 90s this movie was THE epic sci-fi fantasy movie while growing up in that era. It would show practically every summer on our local TV and even with a runtime of three hours long (with advertisements) my brother and I devoured it with a passion that we were never to experience again. I read critics joke that director James Cameron was: Therefore The Abyss was the product of those desires as it is sometimes condescendingly referred to as Close Encounters of the Third Kind…….Underwater. Regardless of the comparison after recently rewatching both movies I consider, by a thin margin, The Abyss to be the superior movie (because Richard Dreyfuss' character in Encounters is an annoying twat.) In the film, a team of divers, scientists, Navy SEALS and the like is sent to recover a sunken submarine and in the process encounter some strange activity. Unlike Encounters I love all the characters in The Abyss and find them all believable and likable. There are so many plotholes in Encounters that anybody with at least a high school education would find several scenes questionable. (So the Government has made so much effort to hide a top secret alien meeting mission from the public yet some crazy, deadbeat dad manages to evade helicopters, highly trained defense force operatives and scale a mountain with a grieving, frantic mom on tow so he could jump aboard a spacecraft of intergalactic kidnappers whose sole intention are to breed hideous human-alien hybrid children…….all so he doesn't have to pay child support.) Jokes aside, I think in retrospect Spielberg bit off far too much than he could chew. He never worked in top secret Government operatives so the story is a bit far fetched. Cameron on the other hand is a professional deep sea explorer so the movie doesn't go too far off the suspension of disbelief scale into ludicrousness. Both movies have stunning finales but I would personally go with The Abyss in terms of scale and wonder whereas Encounters is more impressive in terms of special effects. Sadly The Abyss is hardly ever mentioned and is on the road to becoming a lost classic. At least in my book.

Question: I have a fiance who is living in Portugal. I met him in a dating site, and we communicate in my WhatsApp. I want to video call him, but he said Portugal is banned in video calls. Is that true?
Answer: My 66 year old Aunt had similar circumstances. Recently divorced and living alone far from any family in Ontario she was befriended online by a guy claiming to be working in the US Army. For months they have a back and forth on WhatsApp. She constantly asking for him to take some time to visit her, he constantly reminding her that his army duties don't all for him to vacation as often as he'd like. He also refused all WhatsApp audio and video calls because, according to him, it would compromise the US Army. However he did send her a photo of himself. Coincidentally if you search ‘US Army Officer Facebook’ on Google you can easily come across his photo. He assured her that when he does come and see her he would do so while flying through the skies in the Army helicopter and he would most definitely land in her apartment parking lot and take her up for a ride. She became smitten by him and he asked for her hand in marriage. She agreed but not long after he explained that he was tied up in a court battle over unpaid child support. According to him he had a mission in Somalia and had a rendezvous with one of the local women who eventually got pregnant for him and gave birth to son. My aunt, being as scrupulous as she is, asked for photo evidence of this child. He sent her this thumbnail. Coincidentally his son's photo could be found by simply searching ‘cute Somalian boy’ on Google. Nevertheless my aunt was convinced by his evidence and impressed by the cuteness of his son. Her Army boyfriend persuaded her to send $5000 CAD to the child's mother's Somalian bank account. After she did as such (and after being a bit wary as to why he was so adamant to remind her to send it on a daily basis) she stopped recieving messages from him. She came to the conclusion that she was scammed. It deeply hurt her and embarassed her and caused her sons and ex husband to stop sending her any large sums of money. However luck would have it that she befriended through Facebook a Swedish doctor of Indian descent. While discovering that he came into inheritance of a large sum of money he asked for her hand in marriage. Unfortunately, while on his way to see her he was held by Belgian authorities in regards to his large stash of gold in his suitcase in which he's now asking my aunt for help with his legal fees. Because of this unique situation he is unable to send or receive WhatsApp video calls. No matter how much we've tried to convince my aunt to drop this obvious scam she wouldn't listen. Anyway my point being is that whenever you meet some exotic character online who tells you some wacky story with claims that can be disproved with a simple Google search, it is with 100% certainty that person is trying to scam you.

Question: What is wrong with parents these days that they don’t teach their kids manners & respect?
Answer: About a year ago a teacher brought a parent to me. The parent was a mother of two of the most atrocious girls in the school. These were girls who got into fights, provoked others into fighting through taunting and accusing on social media, disrespected everyone in positions of authority and had a nasty, defiant attitude in general. The teacher wanted the parent to get an overall view of all the trouble these girls caused and how desperately they were in need of an intervention. As a librarian for the school library I had had a few bad encounters with the girls so seeing that the mother was there waiting patiently for my story (and wearing a T-shirt that showed that she worked for the police service) I was only too glad to give her the details of my experience and my hope for these girls and their future. After about 2 minutes of recounting my experience with them and making impassioned pleas I glanced at the mother's face and noticed that there was not a trace of emotion. There was an awkward silence as I waited for her to say something. 'Is that all?’ she said with an irritated tone. 'Yes' I replied. 'Did they do anything to you personally?’ she added. 'No. It's not about me. It's about the library…..it's about the school.’ There was another pause. 'So are you banning them from your library?’ she said. 'No I never said I was banning them from the library.’ With that said she remained silent and stared at me, waiting for me to dismiss the conversation of which I did. She then left with the teacher to talk to another teacher who had had encounters with them. Later that day I heard that that was the formula she applied in all the conversations. She listened to every teacher's complaint and simply waited to hear if any action was going to be taken against her girls. She was pumped and ready to fight anyone who was going to take action against her girls or deny them their ‘rights.’ She had no solutions in her mind as to the problems the girls caused because in her mind there were no problems. The girls were defiant against the school system because the mother was defiant against the system. The mom's attitude was that the school system and its rules were a big joke; that all kids behaved like her daughters behaved and she was not having her daughters victimised. So my answer to all this is parents don't teach manners and respect to their kids because they don't believe in the system and they think they are entitled to their own set of rules to live by.

Question: What is the most pathetic thing you have witnessed in your life? Share?
Answer: I worked pizza delivery while the State oil refinery PETROTRIN went bust. 5000+ workers were sent home. This may seem sad but bear in mind the State owned refinery was rife with corruption, wastage, poor governance and terrible decision making, accruing a staggering debt that increased each year to the height of 12 Billion TT (1.7 Billion US) before it closed for good. Regardless of its obvious problems the company, the management and its union didn't stop to consider this but went ahead paying exorbitant salaries. The average worker got $45,000 a month. Temporary workers got $21,000 a month. Cleaners got $10,000 a month. When they went on strike they were paid while striking and the company brought in temporary workers who were paid close to the amount of permanent workers. This went on until the strikers decided to stop. A carpenter made $70,000 in overtime in just one month. All of this for a company that didn't see a profit for several years. The last thought that seemed to register on these workers' minds was whether something had to be done to address this wanton wastage. In fact the last unified effort they made before closure was a fight for an increase in wages. I worked two jobs at the time. I worked in a public office by day and did pizza delivery by night. Even with two jobs, with maximum overtime and tips, I wouldn't make a quarter of what the average PETROTRIN worker made each month. But here is the most pathetic encounter ever witnessed by myself and the fine staff at the pizza restaurant I worked: A guy came in with his family on a busy Saturday. In his hand was a thick wad of papers. They were meal vouchers from PETROTRIN. PETROTRIN, in another of its wanton carefree spending measures, allowed for workers to get a voucher for a meal valued approx $40 for each time someone worked overtime. This guy apparently never redeemed his vouchers and came with a year's worth to our restaurant. He knew that in time our restaurant would ban those vouchers as all the other popular food places had done so he decided to cash in all, right then and there, to anyone who was stupid enough to accept these worthless pieces of paper. The combined vouchers had a value of over $2000. The guy wanted to redeem them all. He had a smug look of bitter resolve on his face. His wife looked embarrassed and apologetic towards us while the 10yo son looked confused. The man spoke in raised tones to the cashier when she said she would have to speak to the manager. The manager came and explained that in the history of our restaurant we never had a situation like this. We were all aware that PETROTRIN went bust and there was no chance of the company redeeming us for these vouchers. The man barked at the manager that the vouchers were valid and he was ready to take legal action if we refused them (I rolled my eyes). The wife kept trying to calm the husband down. She seemed exceedingly humiliated by the whole affair but the man persisted. In the end the manager acquiesced. The man ordered something like 8 pizzas, 6 salads and 5 artisan sandwiches. The hubbub caused a queue to form and when they got wind of what was happening, they started angrily protesting for the man to hurry up. However, instead of being thankful that we obliged his worthless vouchers, the guy stubbornly and defiantly decides to pull out his calculator and check his order against his voucher total. He sees that he has $7 remaining. 'How much for one of those donuts?’ he looks at me and asks. 'Six dollars,' I reply stoically. 'And gimme one of those donuts,' he said, 'Any one of them.’ The manager meanwhile was reading the vouchers and then saw something suspicious. She noticed that they were supposed to be signed off by a supervisor. None of them were signed off. Also, they were all consecutively numbered (as in 10,020 straight up to 10,050 with no missing vouchers in between). Also, for supposedly old vouchers they all had that neat, uncreased look. It was obvious that the guy ripped them all out from a voucher booklet and stole them when nobody was looking. However, the manager simply mentioned that the vouchers are irredeemable because they were not signed off. The man throws a tantrum and storms off to his vehicle. Five minutes later he comes back with them all signed. He lies and says that his supervisor was in the area. Practically everyone in the restaurant stares at the man in disgust, even his wife. He folds his arms defiantly. The manager acquiesces again and within thirty minutes he leaves with his massive order. Obviously he and his family would not be able to eat all but wastage is something that he is accustomed to. I look at the guy leaving and feel disgusted. Rather than accept his position with grace he instead choses to become even more bitter, corrupt and deceitful. I felt sorry for the the guy's son who is being taught to milk everything for what it's worth and feel entitled to take advantage of everyone around you, especially when the milk and honey stops flowing
