Question: What one thing did your father do that left your mother sobbing?
Answer: Wasn't my biological father but my stepfather. Calling him 'stepfather’ is a bit of a compliment. He basically lived off my mom, was unemployed more often than not and barely provided anything for the rent free roof that lay above his head. Yet my mother persevered. She got involved with my biological father at a tender age and that relationship was traumatic due to his bipolar disorder. She was intent on having a proper family with my stepfather, especially after she bore him two daughters. As mentioned before he was more often unemployed and when when he did find a job it was temporary as he worked in construction. However, in the early 2000s he found some measure of success in the field and started getting established as a professional foreman. He got high paying, big contract jobs and had the power to hire and fire. Soon most of the guys in the street were given jobs by my stepfather and some of the neighborhood women sent love letters in the mailbox to my mother's ire. My stepfather would laugh it off. However as the months turned into years my mother calculated that with the amount of money my stepfather made, it wasn't reflected in the household. We were still broke, had almost no furniture, bills still piled up and the money he gave her was not any significant improvement to when he was roughing it. Things got worse when my stepfather would constantly disappear for the fortnight weekend, especially when he got his salary. When he gave my mother what scanty money remained in his wallet it led to ugly arguments. Everyone told my mother that my stepfather had to be seeing another woman. My mother refused to believe it. Instead she tried to nag, quarrel and harrass him into doing what was right and it just created more nasty arguments. She then resolved that he could no longer live with us but could see his daughters on the weekend. She believed this would change his ways. He readily agreed to this. One fateful Friday evening I was home and the phone rang. I answered it. I heard my stepfather's voice asking for 'Tracey.’ Tracey was the name of our neighbor's daughter. She was 24 years old and had a reputation. I said Tracey didn't live here. When my stepfather recognized my voice he immediately hung up the phone. My mother came and asked me who called. 'It's just S****n.’ 'What does he want?’ my mother said irritably. 'I dunno,' I replied, 'He just asked to talk to Tracey….I think he dialled the wrong number.’ At 16 years old I was a bit naive to comprehend what all this meant. However I'd never forget seeing my mother's face drop like she saw death materialize in front of her and later tears formed in her eyes. My stepfather was getting involved with our neighbor's daughter right across the street. That's where his money went. That meant everyone knew about it except her. That meant she was a fool. They parted ways permanently afterwards. My stepfather would demand that I say that I was mistaken. That it wasn't him who called. He's 68 now and his daughters want nothing to do with him. It really affected my mother as she became more withdrawn and a bit of a recluse and a hoarder. They both are barely on speaking terms. Sometimes I feel as though I should've had more common sense and just kept my mouth shut.

Question: What was your first clue you were no longer as young as you thought you were?
Answer: While working in a school library I was at the computers assisting some students in finishing their assignments to submit to their teachers. Most students would email their assignments to their teacher, others (who didn't have/couldn't remember their email address) would save it on a USB flash drive . This one student who had neither an email address or a flash drive raised his hand for assistance and told me of his situation. I went into our storage cupboard and brought out an old rewritable CD-RW; the kind I used back in school to copy (‘burn’ as we used to call it) data onto. I gave him the shiny disc and walked off assuming that he knew what to do with it. ‘Sir!’ I heard his voice call after me. ‘Yeah?’ ‘What am I supposed to do with this?’ ‘Burn it,’ I said and looked at him stoically. His friends started laughing believing that I was teasing. ‘Sir stop joking. I need to save my work.’ ‘Burn the work onto the CD’ I said and he started to look at me irritated. ‘Sir help him out. Stop joking’ one of the friends said. It then dawned on me that they had no idea what ‘burning a CD’ was. This was before their time. I proceeded to demonstrate to them how to copy data onto a CD-RW, feeling like a crusty old man giving them a tour on a private railroad. The sad thing was they were all 16–17 and I wasn't much older at 24.

Question: What's the most dishonest thing you've experienced in your working life?
Answer: In a school I once worked there was on old curmudgeon who worked as a handyman. For simplicity’s sake I'll refer to him as Levi. Everything about him was dishonest. He was employed as a handyman but could barely repair anything. Any minor problem brought to him, he make it seem as though it were was a huge issue. We had a toilet that gave problems to flush. We told him about it and without flushing and inspecting it, he claimed that the entire toilet was broken and needed to be replaced. He actually managed to get the Principal to sign off on this and any other 'replace’ verdicts he claimed as he knew how to charm women in high positions. He would then 'discard’ of the old toilet or any other item that was replaced. He was a talker and a social butterfly. He would always rant about how hard his life was. He lived to blow smoke up people's asses. Whenever you saw him he always 'just came back from a smoke...' I interpreted this by mentally adding '…up someone's ass’ to his statement. Whenever anyone discussed work with him he would always say his mantra, 'There's no incentive here for me.’ Everyone knew he was corrupt and took advantage of the job and the Principal. Because he was a character with personality and didn't rip-off his fellow workers with his incentives, everyone still liked him. However his desire for more incentives was to get the better of us. The school had a hill of old, beaten up iron and aluminium student chairs. They were stored outside the building in the back. They were an eyesore for the school and especially for the Principal. The Principal wanted to get rid of them but because of auditing purposes she couldn't simply discard them without approval from her district supervisor and a whole bunch of red tape. Levi saw the hill of chairs as a goldmine. He would tell everyone how much it would be worth as scrap iron and made his ultimate incentive to be to get the permission to discard of those chairs. One day he came to me with a proposal. I had a pickup. He told me that the principal gave him permission to discard of the chairs. He wanted me to take them to the scrapyard and we'd split the money 50:50. Knowing that he was a con-artist I went to the Principal and asked if she indeed gave him permission. She confirmed it was true and if I could assist with the transport. I agreed to the proposal. Levi also hired one of the junior handymen for a flat rate. Myself and the junior handyman worked ourselves to the core stacking those chairs to the van and securing. Levi didn't lift a finger as he complained about his old age and his back. It took three trips with my pickup to carry all the chairs to the scrapyard. By the time we were done, the junior handyman and I were dripping in sweat. We waited outside the building to get our cut from Levi. When Levi finally came out he was shouting racial obscenities against the entire Chinese population. We asked him what happened. He said that the owner, a native of China, could barely speak English and inspected the entire haul with the conclusion of 'Iron no good. We want aluminium.’ Levi said that the Chinese owner didn't want the iron chairs, practically 95% of the the haul, but only the aluminium ones which had a higher market value. He said the owner wanted us to carry the iron ones back. Levi said he begged the man to take the iron chairs for whatever price he was willing to offer. We asked Levi how much money he got for the entire haul. Levi showed us $75TT from his wallet. We were stunned. I for one didn't believe Levi's story in the least. I went inside to talk to the owner. Unfortunately it was true that he barely spoke English. We couldn't understand each other and he simply said to me, 'Iron no good. Next time bring aluminium.’ Levi acted the most heartbroken of all. All that work for nothing. We split the money in three. The junior handyman lamented that he never worked so hard in his life for enough money to buy a pack of cigarettes. A few weeks later Levi stopped coming to work. When the school rang him he announced that he was taking early retirement. The principal called me into her office all of a sudden. 'Where are the chairs?’ she cried, 'The supervisor is coming tomorrow.’ I told her I didn't understand what she meant. She explained to me that she gave Levi permission to salvage whatever chairs he could from the pile, have them repaired and painted and in exchange he could 'discard’ the rest. I told her the arrangement Levi had with us and how we carried all the chairs to the scrapyard. She stared at me with fury. She asked me if I knew where Levi lived. I said no. She said her calls to him went straight to voice message. She cried that Levi was supposed to bring 23 refurbished chairs for her since last week. She even had the figure listed in the school inventory. I didn't know what to tell her. I said I would try to find out any information I could. I called the scrapyard to find out if they had any information on him: a second phone number, an address etc. Thankfully the Chinese owner had a English speaking person employed as a CSR. I asked the CSR about Levi and whether she has any information on him. She looked up our sale in the computer. She said Levi made the transaction under the school's name and phone number but left no personal information on himself other than his first name. I then found out that the sale of the chairs as scrap amounted to almost $3000TT. Levi had ripped everyone off, myself, the junior handyman, the Principal and the school. Big time. Looks like he had finally gotten his incentive.

Question: Would Hollywood actor Brad Pitt have made it in old or classic Hollywood back in the day?
Answer: Very interesting question. For the sake of simplification let's just assume that by Classic Hollywood you mean the Hays Code era of Hollywood whereas sex, nudity, graphic violence, rape etc could not be demonstrated in Hollywood films. (1934 — 1968) 1930s — 1940s Hollywood Hollywood in the aftermath of the Great Depression and the outbreak of the Second World War. This is the age of the Go-Getter and although silent movies are now obsolete, it's exaggerative stage acting style is still rampant. Audiences of this era are favorable towards a certain type of male screen presence. Popular actors of the era are mostly an embodiment of what were considered desirable, manly traits. This is the era of Clark Gable, Cary Grant, Gary Cooper, James Stewart, Errol Flynn, John Wayne and Henry Fonda. The archetypal male film star was usually tall (over 6 feet), athletic, handsome, possessing a rich and resonant voice and possessing a certain self assured alpha male quality. The kind of man who would've made a great career as a top salesman or workforce motivator. The nation was wounded after two World Wars and these idealistic tropes were coveted by men and women alike. It was an age that was obsessively preoccupied with courage, persistence and survival. It was the era of sucking in your emotions and holding your chin high. Unless in possession of exemplary acting skills or song and dance expertise, actors who lacked several of these traits were relegated to minor supporting roles, comic relief roles, extras, stunt work or failed to make it in the film industry at all. Despite being ruggedly handsome, Brad Pitt would've had a hard time getting work in Hollywood during this era. He did not fit the height requirement, his voice would not be considered rich and animated and his brooding, sombre presence would've been a turn off for a national audience hungry for the next cocky, high shouldered, go-getting macho man. 1950s Hollywood The ideal aforementioned leading man is still prevalent with Charlton Heston, Gregory Peck, Burt Lancaster, and Rock Hudson maintaining the status quo. However standards are less rigid as actors like William Holden, Frank Sinatra, Kirk Douglas, Yul Brynner and Tony Curtis, who have the macho appeal but lack the height, are some of the top stars. A growing interest in brooding more sensitive type 'method' acting is gaining ground with the likes of James Dean, Marlon Brando and Paul Newman. Brad Pitt would've been better able to find work in such type roles but the competition would be fierce and only those with extensive stage experience and schooled in New York at the Actor's Studio would get top priority over some quiet, good looking guy from Missouri. 1960s Hollywood The growing counterculture revolution is finally making an impact on Hollywood. While the war scarred older generation is fading to make way for the Baby Boomers, the conservative values and ideal macho leading man is no longer as appealing for those hungry for emotional catharsis. The audience is yearning for a leading man who they could relate to, who shares their flaws and can demonstrate vulnerability. Even the more macho type actors are expected to demonstate weakness and more sensitivity. These would include Clint Eastwood, Sean Connery, Charles Bronson, Steve McQueen, Robert Redford, George Kennedy and Rod Steiger. Slurred speaking (Marlon Brando), meek voiced (Eastwood) overweight (Steiger) and short stature (Bronson) are traits no longer shunned by Hollywood elite. Brad Pitt would've found the greatest chance of obtaining prominent roles during this era. Who knows he might've even replaced Robert Redford in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

Question: Have you ever had a bad church experience?
Answer: Some years ago, I was interested in a girl I met through a friend. Let's just call her Lula. Lula was highly religious and she subtly let me know that she was not dating a man unless he 'walked with Jesus.’ I decided that I should indeed become reacquainted with God as I hadn't been to church in several years. She invited me to her church. She was a member of its Youth Group, SRRCY or the San Raphael Roman Catholic Youth. The church was located in a small town in the countryside called San Raphael. I came there after work on a Tuesday around 6pm. The congregation was quite small. Apart from the Youth Group members, there were only five other people, myself included. The youth members all wore SRRCY labelled polos in green or blue. Before the service began many of them came to me, one by one, to welcome and make idle chatter, each bearing a wide smile. They all asked the same question at some point in time: 'Did you bring anyone with you?’ Each time I replied in the negative they would advise me to bring a friend, family or coworkers next time I came. I saw Lula upfront and sat next to her. I was expecting to see a bright smile and get a warm welcome but instead she gave me a confused look and said, 'You didn't bring anyone with you?’ I explained to her that my family weren't keen to attend church on a Tuesday but she didn't seem to be listening so I became faintly annoyed. The service then began with the priest giving a sermon on redemption. He was likable and spoke in a down-to-earth, informal style and related personal stories rather than Bible verses. He asked if there was anyone new in the congregation. Myself and two other guys raised our hands. We were asked to introduce ourselves. I went first and gave my name Elijah (which they cheered for as it's a Biblical name). I explained that I wanted to get closer with God and that I hadn't been to church in ages. When I sat down Lula glared at me angrily and asked why I didn't let everyone know that she was the one who invited me to the church. I wondered what was the big deal when I noticed the other two guys name-drop their inviters while introducing themselves which made me lose points with Lula. Then things started to take a turn for the surreal. One of the youth members, a thin, sickly looking girl around age 23 who sat on the same pew with us started to shake and convulse. She fell to the ground and started to foam at the mouth while uttering indecipherable gibberish in a vicious tone. Instead of telling everyone to clear the way and give this poor, delirious girl some air while he called the ambulance, the priest told the SRRCY to gather around her and pray for her. They all gathered around her while she twisted and contorted her body while sticking out her tongue at the SRRCY and laughing maniacally while they said their prayers. Honestly, I felt a bit frightened. I watched Lula as she pulled out her rosary, bent down and held the possessed girl by the back of the head and started praying intensely. The possessed girl made some nasty gurgling noises and all of a sudden Lula's phone began to ring with the ringtone of Robin Thicke's Blurred Lines. It was quite a macabre yet awkwardly funny sight to behold this possessed girl twisting and squealing while Blurred Lines played in the background. Finally Lula grew angry and paused her prayers to whip out her phone and angrily sent a WhatsApp text to whomever was calling her. After resuming her prayers, the demon was exorcised about two minutes later. ~~~~~~~~ Twenty minutes after the service was ended. The possessed girl had resumed her place on the pew as though having Satan exorcised from her body was as common as recovering from belly cramps. She even had a healthy glow about her. They SRRCY all got together and congratulated each other for another good service and they went around with the priest reminding everyone to bring more people with them next time they arrived. I volunteered to give Lula a ride home. However she and the rest of the SRRCY stood having idle chatter at the entrance of the building for ages. Even the formerly possessed girl, who only a few minutes ago, was on the ground contorting and blaspheming in an unknown demon-language was there chatting in good spirits. Finally they decided to part and Lula hopped in my van. While I drove she asked how I found the experience. I replied that it definitely changed my views on certain churches, priests and church youth groups. I didn't elaborate on what I meant by that because I noticed that she wasn't even paying attention. Her phone was ringing again. Edit 1.11.21 Thank you for all the upvotes. A commenter asked for a link to the parish and in doing so I've managed to glean some photos from their Facebook page. Feel free to comment your thoughts. Two characters from my story. Can you guess who?

Question: What's the biggest anticlimax in movie history?
Answer: Bird Box (2018) was throughly gripping. All the characters were well fleshed out and relatable and as ridiculous as the premise was (unseen, omnipresent entities that makes one commit suicide if seen) the suspense and horror was so effective it became the most streamed Netflix film at the time, mostly due to word of mouth. SPOILER ALERT But by God what a stupid ending. After so much trauma in the first half of the film, years later Sandra Bullock’s character Malorie and her children (one biological, one adopted) are rowing blindfolded down a dangerous river to find the people who sent her a transmission as to a safe location. After a nail biting odyssey down the river we are all expecting to be given answers when she finally arrives at this mysterious, resistance base. What are those creatures? Where did they come from? What do they want? Why do people kill themselves just by looking at them? What is the state of the world right now? Do the entities have a weakness, is it possible to fight back? Instead the movie does the most dirty tactic that a studio could possible do. Instead of providing the audience what they waited for and dedicated our energy and emotions toward (answers) the studio goes the cheap route and decides to end the film by answering nothing, leaving the film open to sequels and prequels. This is a trend I’ve noticed in a lot of modern horrors and thrillers. They just can't end the effing movie and give us the closure that we waited two hours for. Ranting aside, Malorie reaches the destination, a school for the blind and everyone assures her that everything will be ok in one of the most corniest and cliched endings ever conceived. It’s a pity Malorie didn’t wake up from a dream and see all the familiar faces around her while uttering ‘There’s no place like home.’ I would’ve much appreciated that ending than the actual ending of Bird Box.

Question: What happened to your school bully?
Answer: He had a wonderful transformation. He did a complete 360 from being a LITTLE piece of s**t to a BIG piece of s**t. Back in school there was none more despised than Akeem. He was (still is) quite short (probably 5′6 at most) and dare I say, not one of the better looking boys in class. He deeply desired friends/attention and being that he was neither funny nor pleasant he realized that he could only make a name for himself by instilling fear. Being short, skinny and devoid of athleticism, he knew that he couldn’t cause physical damage to anyone. Instead, he developed a remarkable talent in calling classmates out on anything remotely embarrassing or hurtful about their lives. If you wore hand-me-down clothing… If your father had mental problems and periods of homelessness… If your mother had a gap in her teeth… If your family was on welfare… If you couldn’t afford to buy food in the cafeteria and relied on school feeding programs… If you depended on the free bus service to get home… you had to be sure to NEVER let Akeem get wind of that information because it would be guaranteed that he would make a public announcement of it. ‘Darcelle, you smell like that cheap Him n’ Her unisex deodorant. You don’t feel ashamed to be a female wearing cheap deodorant? How about everybody put up money to get Darcelle some decent deodorant for her birthday?’ ‘Look Elijah’s wearing the same shirt his brother wore to school yesterday.’ ‘Hey Benny. Maybe the principal could pick up your father at the gas station for the Parent-Teacher meeting. Isn’t that where he begs?’ That was his shtick. He would sit all day in class and pick a random person to taunt and reveal something dreadfully sad or embarrassing about their life that he carefully and methodically deduced or discovered through prying. Of course there were kids that he would dare not provoke, the ones who would knock out his teeth if he attempted rip on them. The rest of the class, practically had to avoid eye contact with him during a free period in fear that he say something nasty about their home, mother, father, siblings etc. This attitude of his continued for the duration of his school tenure. Fast forward twenty years later and I see that I’m being followed on Instagram by someone with whom I have a lot of mutual friends. Upon closer inspection I observe that it’s Akeem. I tell myself that maybe he’s trying to reach out to old classmates and show how much he’s changed into a better individual. I couldn't be more wrong. No. Akeem was more interested in showboating bling and lifestyle. He was simply networking, with a little showing off on the side. I looked for any photo that didn't scream 'Bet you never drove/been on/wore/visited this,’ a photo that demonstrated a more subtle side to him, and the most I could find was a photo of him sticking his tongue on his wife's face. But say what, everyone is responsible for his own destiny. According to his Instagram he rents luxury vehicles so lemme be the bigger man and plug his Instagram business/personal link for your enjoyment. You will see for yourself what a wonderful guy he grew up to be.

Question: Do you believe in "white privilege"? Have you ever witnessed/experienced it?
Answer: If I could humbly present examples of ‘white privilege’ I've observed here in the Caribbean. This is my father's friend Z (on the right). He is a white Trinidadian who happens to be poor. The area around him is at his house. He lives in a shed in the mountains with no running water or electricity. No. He is not a hippie or a hermit. It is through circumstance that he lives in such conditions. He had a period of his life where he was addicted to drugs and lived on the streets. He has turned his life around and now seasonally plants tomatoes for the person whose land he lives on. I've hung out with Z several times. He has a humble, salt of the earth type mindset and humour and is greatly appreciative of the little things in life (a decent meal, a hammock, a glass of cold water etc). At no point in my life have I ever seen ‘white privilege’ directed his way and I don't expect to. Z doesn't have a refined way of speaking, his clothes are always rough and oversized and he carries with him the scent of cheap perfume. People here notice his skin for a few seconds and when he opens his mouth that's where his privilege ends. Z is an anomaly because he is ‘white’ (skin colour, physical features etc) and ‘not white’ at the same time (speech, clothing, mannerisms etc). If that makes any sense. This is T. She is another white Trinidadian. I befriended her on a trip to Dominica in 2011. She came from a stable family but she herself was not someone who lived in comfort let alone possessed any measure of wealth. However, unlike the above mentioned Z, she was brought up to learn and demonstrate a certain refined image and social graces. She dressed well, spoke articulate and carried about herself like a cultured lady of means despite being in the lower-middle class bracket. T demonstrated her ‘white privilege’ to me one evening. At a beach our hiking group visited there was a rather nice hotel. Feeling adventurous we climbed the stairs to the hotel and saw that it took us to a stately but empty dining area overlooking the beach. Afraid that we would be unceremoniously kicked out I was suggesting we head back down the stairs. However T wanted to show me something. She told me to sit at a table and be quiet. She sat opposite me pretending to browse a menu. Within a few minutes a waiter arrived. He questioned as to what we would like to have. T said that she hadn't decided yet. The waiter, not annoyed in the least, asked if we would like any complimentary refreshments. T asked if it was possible we could have sparkling wine as the refreshment. The waiter said that usually soda or water was the complimentary refreshment but he would see what he could do. He came afterwards with some glasses and a bottle of sparkling wine which he poured for us both. He left the bottle with us and said that he would be available whenever we were ready. We pretended to browse the menu while drinking the wine. I whispered to her that now we would have to buy something or the waiter would make a scene. She laughed at my statement and said that she always did this on every island she visited. Sometimes she was even given free entrées as well just for looking the part of a respectable white woman. After we drank we left without a word I partook for a moment in her white privilege: being offered free sparkling wine at a hotel and not being chased off after not buying anything. And finally, this gentleman here was a family member of mine. I say was because he passed away over 20 years ago. He is quite clearly a white male individual. My memory of him is limited but from the best I can recall he was a booming, boisterous and charismatic man who worked odd jobs and semi skilled labour driving around in a pick up truck looking for work. His white privilege was that for a brief period of his life he got a lot of temporary but decent paying jobs (pressure washing buildings, cleaning windows etc) at greater ease than colored people looking for such jobs. However it has been said that he became an addict and from then on his downfall became rapid: divorce, losing custody of his son and then rejection in his job/personal endeavours. He fell on serious hard times, suffered from crippling depression and was found dead in his cramped apartment (details of which I cannot divulge). None of the above three examples experienced any significant favourable treatment in their lives other than a few inconsequential perks every so often. A complimentary glass of sparkling wine and a job to clean someone's windows can hardly be called ‘white privilege.’ Privilege is what happens due to factors that usually involve wealth, status and beauty, and it occurs in all races in all countries. So in conclusion in Trinidad and the greater Caribbean, there is a large degree of ‘white perks’ but I'm yet to see any significant examples of ‘white privilege.’

Question: Do you think Europe is more racist than the USA?
Answer: I haven't been to the whole of Europe and I haven't travelled all the States of the USA. However I've been to Wales and Kentucky recently and I've had two encounters that I think could be used as data towards answering the above question. Aberystwyth, Wales. I was a student on a scholar for a Masters degree along with a few fellow Trinidadians. When we went out shopping, our favourite store by far was Poundland. We patronized Poundland almost on a daily basis buying chocolates, sweets and various goodies for a pound each to our hearts’ delight. Despite the noticeable frigidity of many people in the area we saw, most were helpful and polite. One day at Poundland I was informed that there were rewards to anyone with purchases of over £25 pounds and up. The more you spent the better the reward. After shopping I checked my receipt and saw that I qualified to redeem a cool digital sports watch. I went over to the guy at customer service and showed my receipt. People from Aberystwyth tend to wear a constant smile that fluctuates from smile to smirk according to the mood/situation. This guy's smile changed to a definite smirk when he saw me waving my receipt. ‘What’s that you say?’ he said as though I were speaking Swahili. ‘I want to get the watch.’ I repeated for the third time, ‘I spent over thirty pounds.’ He watched me waving my receipt with a confused expression on his face as though I were a lunatic waving a bill of rights. ‘Come again?’ he said and I knew he was playing stupid and I started to get annoyed. I notice that he's glancing towards the back of the store as if to communicate to the others that he wanted someone else to come over. Suddenly an older man came towards us and asked what was the problem. I explained that I wanted to redeem my points for the sports watch. I showed him the receipt but he stares at me up and down instead. ‘You’re not from the UK I would guess,’ he says. I said no, that I was here on studies. He hemmed and hawed and then said that the prizes are meant for UK citizens. I told him that there was no mention of that in the advertisement hanging on the wall next to him. He hemmed and hawed again and said that it may not be written in the ad but the promotion is to encourage locals to shop at Poundland more. I asked to speak to the manager and with a smirk he said, ‘Nice to meet you. I'm the manager Steve.’ Him and the other worker then proceeded to stare at me, brandishing their wide smile-smirks. Deciding not to make a ruckus I left the matter at that. Georgetown, Kentucky I visited my girlfriend and we stopped at the police station at the above location for her to deal with a matter. While I was waiting for her in the car I grew bored after 30 minutes. There was a swarm of bees that surrounded the area and as they left I went out to take a video of them as the swarmed off. A police car rolls up about 20 feet away from me and the driver's window rolls down. A latino officer then smiles at me and says ‘Hey.’ I said Hi. He says something else but I couldn't hear him so I went closer to his vehicle. He asks me what I was doing there in the car park and I explained that I was waiting for a friend inside the station. He asked me where I was from and I explained that I was from the Caribbean. Suddenly another police car comes speedily from the opposite direction and parks in an aggressive manner as if to cut me off from running away. A tall stocky Caucasian officer exits the vehicle and comes towards me and demands that I keep my hands away from my pockets. He proceeds to search me and discovers me unarmed. He explains that someone reported me as a suspicious individual hanging around the police station parking lot. I explained that I was just a tourist from the Caribbean. They explained that loitering about a police station is seen as suspicious in the State of Kentucky and that I should remain in my vehicle if I waited on my friend here. Tall stocky guy stares at me and asks if I have any questions myself. I said no but I said I appreciated how alert they were and if only Trinidad had such dedicated officers we would have less crime. They both laugh awkwardly and stocky guy pats me on my shoulder like a schoolkid. They both leave without another word. In conclusion I would honestly say that my experience in Wales seemed to border more on seething racism rather my experience in Kentucky. I believe the officers in Georgetown were doing their job whilst the staff at Poundland at Aberystwyth were discriminating in a subtle manner. There was a certain deep seated resentment I felt in Wales whilst in Kentucky it was more of a passive wariness. I felt as though I could've communicated to the officers and reach a certain compromise whilst with the Poundland staff I felt like a brick wall was between us. I also felt like that with the locals of Kentucky, a friendly warmth while in Aberystwyth it was an air of cold professionalism for the most part. In rural Kentucky, places like Kuttawa and Paducah I got no strange looks and witnessed black people working alongside whites in seeming normalcy whereas in Aberystwyth the one black person I witnessed was a homeless man and the one mixed race person was young man working in a thrift shop. So in my honest and ignorant opinion I would think that racism would be more prevalent in a subtle, passive aggressive manner in Europe whilst in the US it can happen due to wariness of strangers rather than due to race. Edit: There is one commenter who continuously alleges that I’ve fabricated my story about my visit to Wales and Aberystwyth. Every time I reply with evidence to him it somehow disappears so I’ve decided to put the evidence where it can’t be removed here in the answer.

Question: Who was the weirdest kid in your class?
Answer: Ray was the weirdest boy I ever met in my life. To this day I’ve never come across a boy so profoundly odd as this boy Ray who was a classmate of mine. His story is somewhat of a sad one as he was a slow student from a really poor background. Ray had a learning deficiency and was kept down some grades, making him two years older than the rest of us. He had an early growth spurt and at age 11, he could pass for a stocky and pudgy young man. This made him look absolutely ridiculous in our school uniform. Him squeezing into our generic blue shirt/khaki shorts ensemble and with his socks pulled high upon his leg reminded me of those silly yodeling Bavarian men I would see on TV advertisements. To make it worse. Ray would never stop smiling. He had to his credit an indefatigable attitude towards life. No matter how many insults were thrown his way (by both teachers and students), no matter how often he was bullied or was ignored when football/cricket teams were chosen or was screamed at by his teacher, the principal etc, he would simply smile and laugh away the matter. Ray would’ve made a first rate boxer if he had chosen that direction in life. I saw Ray take several punches in play fights and not a single grimace of pain would appear on his face. During a lunch period several boys made it a game to fling stones to shoo a mangy dog that kept coming near the school for food. Ray who, for some unknown reason, was running around the field by himself ran straight into one of those stones as it collided with his head. He stopped and looked about in a confused manner and then continued running around. No one sat near Ray during class. The teachers endorsed this practice to teach him a lesson to buck up on his schoolwork. Once, I had a falling out with my friends and they told me I was banished from the gang. Angrily, I told them I didn’t care and didn’t need them and went and did the unthinkable. I went and sat next to Ray as the entire class looked on in horror. Ray was absolutely delighted to get a new friend. I feigned interest in being his friend to spite my gang. However, in little time, things started to get weird. I knew Ray was weird but spending the week with him made me realize the extent to his weirdness. Firstly, I accidentally spilt some ink on the desk. I was terrified the teacher would see and I frantically looked for some tissue to wipe the mess. In my amazement I watched as Ray scooped up the ink in his palm and rubbed it into his hair. He smiled and told me that ink gives his hair a good shine. Then we began to discuss our personal lives. I told him the bare basics about my family, as to who it composed of and he immediately began to discuss extremely cringe and taboo subjects about his family such as how he has to help his grandmother wipe her butt after she poos and how he hated when there was a water shortage because his sister had a problem with her, let’s just say ‘personal odors.’ Hearing him speak these things so openly and with a huge smile on his face made me recoil. I decided that conversation was the not the best idea for the two of us. During recess I told Ray that I wanted to be alone for the time being and Ray queried as to why. Ray wanted us two to play ‘Catch’ (Tag) but I explained to him that it would be ridiculous for just two boys to play Catch, that we needed a big group. He then gave me a massive shove that sent me on the ground and started giggling ‘Catch me, catch me.’ He had a very effeminate manner of running and the fact that his pants were way too small and tight made him look atrocious as he giggled and ran around, waiting for me to run after him. My friends saw all this and looked at me with pity and shook their heads in dismay. It all came to an end one morning when my best friend came to me and begged that I return to the gang. I said ‘no way.’ He proceeded to tell me that all the girls and even the teachers were starting to speculate that I was gay and Ray was my boyfriend. With that said I immediately returned to my gang and left Ray in the dust. Sad, but that is how the mindset of an impressionable 9 year old boy can be. I look back in regret at how unintentionally mean I was as a kid and if I were to ever encounter Ray again I would formally apologize for my behavior from decades past. I do hope that he found some measure of success and happiness in his life. But he really was quite a weird kid. Edit 02.02.22 I’ve met several fascinating characters in my youth. Ray was one, this ‘child genius’ named Vachel was another. Click here to read about him.

Question: Is it ethically preferable to leave popcorn bags and soda cups at one's seat after a movie or to throw them out? If everyone disposed of their own trash, it would mean fewer jobs for people at the movie theater.
Answer: I’ve worked as an usher for two major multiplex cinemas. The cinemas I've worked with employed a cleaning crew who came in early at mornings to do the major clean up i.e. having the cinema spotless upon opening hours. Other than that it was the ushers were the ones given the sole responsibility to do the cleaning of all 8 cinemas and environs. After a movie finished we usually had 30 minutes to clear up all the trash and mess before the next showing. Besides that we also performed security duties, customer service relation duties and most of us were trained doing basic projection (‘threading a film’ as we called it) in case a projectionist took a sick day or quit. People were mostly neat and considerate when it came to their trash but there was certain to be the few outliers who left their seats in a disgusting state of scattered popcorn and nachos, spilt cheese and soda etc. We were not expected to be thorough with our clean up but at the same time no customer was to ever sit and feel popcorn under his/her butt, cheese on the arm rest and the stickiness of spilt soda at their feet. Mind you those cinemas were perennially understaffed. Nobody grows up dreaming of becoming the world's greatest usher. Rarely anyone below supervisory level stuck around in the cinema longer than a year. It was teenagers and college students on holiday who usually applied for the job. Many of them would leave after a month. When Big Budget Action Movie with Explosions Part 2 would make its grand summer premiere in the cinema, no patron would stay back to see what the place looked like when the light switched back on after hundreds of hyperactive children, angst riddled teenagers and fatigued parents had left. It would usually be an ugly sight. You and four other overworked and underpaid ushers had 30 minutes to clean up among the 8 cinemas before another batch of hundreds filed in. Keep in mind that you had to ensure little Johnny Mischiefmaker and his buddies didn't try to sneak into another movie after theirs had finished. Ushers were responsible for ensuring paying customers were the ones who sat on each seat. Failure to do this could result in money deducted in your salary. It wasn't uncommon to see one of my fellow workers running with a broom and scoop tucked under their armpits to tear tickets for people entering and then run to make certain another crowd of people from a finished movie exited the building and then run back to the first cinema to finish cleaning with 5 minutes to spare. All this for minimum wage and the ability to see a free movie once a week. Does that sound like a job someone would be desperate to hold on to? By throwing away your trash and keeping your seat relatively clean you are doing such people a great service. They are grateful to you even though they have no idea who you are most of the time. On the contrary if you believe that by being a sloppy bastard, spilling your food and drink and leaving all your trash on the seat and on the floor and have the audacity to claim that in doing so you are ensuring employment. No. You are ensuring the world that idiots still exist. You are making things worse for everyone around you. If everyone had your mentality cinemas would close down for good. So to the person who asked this question. When you walk the street at night and are unfortunate to get mugged, don't get angry with your mugger. With your logic if muggings no longer happened, it would mean fewer jobs for police. Edit: I never expected this answer to get so many views, upvotes and generate so much conversation. I truly appreciate. Please allow me to exploit the appreciation by including links to (kinda) humorous answers further describing my experience working as an usher.

Question: What small detail from a movie do you love?
Answer: So many to choose from in this movie. I’ll go with the more obvious. In So I Married an Axe Murderer (1993) Mike Myers plays the protagonist Charlie. He's a San Francisco native, the son of fiercely patriotic Scottish immigrants, particularly his father (also played by Mike Myers). When he brings his girlfriend Harriet to visit them, he's a bit embarrassed by their rustic simplicity, particularly that of his well intentioned but obnoxious, loud-mouthed father and retires to the bathroom. If you pay close attention you'll notice on the wall of the bathroom door is a dart board on which a photo of Queen Elizabeth is condescendingly taped on, demonstrating the stereotypical Scottish baby boomer/older generation hatred for the English. Also the scene where he is surprised to discover his enigmatic girlfriend Harriet speaks fluent Russian: Harriet: So what? Bright women intimidate you? Charlie (in a sinister voice): No. No. Not at all. But it's a shame I'm going to have to destroy you. Seems like just random dialogue but it's actually a tongue in cheek Cold War spy reference. Right after that Charlie puts on an Eastern European accent and starts dancing ballet. This is not random. This is reference to defected Cold War era Russian ballet dancers such as Baryshnikov and Nureyev. All of this in keeping with the ‘discovering your mysterious partner can speak Russian’ running joke. The movie is crammed full these little details of cultural ‘niche’ humor ranging from European stereotypes, San Francisco bohemians and hipsters, police work misconceptions, Alcatraz prison tours, butchers, fearmongering, aviation, absurdity of the media etc that one can only notice after repeated viewings. One of the many reasons why the movie has grown in cult status over the years. Edit: To all who are arguing in the comments that the photo on the bathroom door is Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother and not Queen Elizabeth (her daughter) and that it’s impossible for a Scottish person to hate the Queen Mother because she was Scottish herself. I appreciate the information but can we just get on with it. The point of the joke is the Scottish hatred of the English (represented by its royalty) so let’s not quibble too much and just appreciate the scene for what it is.
